text:
Cutter Gauthier is the reason everyone is talking about the Ducks. He has 18 points in his last 10 games, he was the NHL's First Star of the Week, and the Orange County Register has the Ducks "soaring behind a scorching Cutter Gauthier." A five-game winning streak ended against Nashville on Wednesday, but Anaheim is 10-8-1 and 6-3-1 over its last ten.

Here's the uncomfortable part. The Ducks have only 45% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) at five on five, and their goals have outrun their chances by about 8.3 this season. Gauthier's 18 points came on chances worth about 10.7, and Tristan Luneau's 11 points in 10 games on chances worth 4.4. That is a lot of finishing to keep up. The top line of Mikael Granlund, Gauthier and Beckett Sennecke has outscored opponents 7-4, but it has been on the wrong side of the chances (42%), and the top pair of Jackson LaCombe and Noah Warren has been outchanced badly too.

The encouraging sign is recent: Anaheim has had 51% of the expected goals over its last ten, an improvement on the season. Our numbers give the Ducks a 56% chance at the playoffs, projecting about 90 points with a wide range. What we're watching is whether the process keeps catching up to the results before the shooting cools.
